keyTerms.definition: Unit 04 of CS229S, covering CUDA and efficient attention.
The evidence label on every lesson claim, here PLANNED with source attribution pending.

recall.question: What unit and sessions anchor this lesson?
recall.answer: Unit cs229s-U04, concepts C01 to C12, calendar-anchored to Week 3, Oct 07 (Hardware Aware Algorithm Design) and Oct 11 (Efficient Attention).

keyTerms.definition: The fixed structure every concept carries, from source and scope to visual units.
The FlashAttention papers (2022, 2023) this lesson is taught from.

recall.question: Do the labs need a GPU?
recall.answer: No: CUDA specifics are taught from the public programming model, no GPU is needed for the labs (CPU emulation).

keyTerms.definition: 32 threads moving in lockstep (SIMT): the scheduling quantum.
One warp taking both sides of a branch: both paths run serially.
A thread group running on one SM, with shared memory.

recall.question: Define warp, block, grid in one line each.
recall.answer: Warp: 32 threads in lockstep. Block: runs on one SM, with shared memory. Grid: all blocks.

recall.question: 1000 threads, blocks of 256. Warps? Blocks?
recall.answer: 32 warps (ceil(1000/32)), 4 blocks (ceil(1000/256)).

recall.question: A kernel with heavy divergence is slow. Name the mechanism.
recall.answer: A split warp executes both branch paths serially, halving throughput for that warp.

keyTerms.definition: Adjacent threads touching adjacent addresses, merging into minimal transactions.
The mental model: 32 riders boarding one bus when they stand together.

recall.question: Define coalesced access in one line.
recall.answer: Thread i reads address base + i: 32 fp32 reads merge into one 128-byte transaction.

recall.question: fp16, stride 8. Transactions per warp?
recall.answer: 32 threads span 512 bytes: 4 transactions.

recall.question: Kernel moves 32x the expected bytes. Name the pattern.
recall.answer: Strided access: stride-32 fp32 touches 32 different cache lines per warp.

keyTerms.definition: Blocking the working set so tiles fit in on-chip memory and get reused.
The mental model: work one tile at a time, loading A and B tiles into shared memory.
On-chip memory holding one A tile plus one B tile.

recall.question: Define tiling in one line.
recall.answer: You cannot lift the whole floor, so you work one tile at a time: load tiles into shared memory, multiply, accumulate, move on.

recall.question: (1024,1024,1024) matmul, tile 64. A HBM reads vs naive?
recall.answer: Naive: each A element read 1024 times. Tiled: reads drop by ~Tk, so ~16x fewer (1024/64).

recall.question: Tiled kernel fails to launch. Name the resource.
recall.answer: Shared memory: a 256x256 fp16 tile pair needs 256 KB, exceeding it.

keyTerms.definition: Block-wide barrier: no thread passes until every thread in the block arrives.
The mental model: the teacher calls everyone to stop until all are here.
A barrier inside divergent control flow: threads that never reach it wait forever.

recall.question: What does __syncthreads guarantee?
recall.answer: No thread passes the barrier until every thread in the block reaches it, so shared-memory writes are visible to all reads after it.

recall.question: 64 threads, barrier cost 20 cycles, 1e6 barriers. Total cycles?
Kernel hangs with a barrier inside an if. Explain.
recall.answer: Divergent barrier: threads that skip the if never reach the barrier, so the others wait forever.

keyTerms.definition: Active warps divided by max warps per SM.
The mental model: an SM holds fixed rooms (warp slots, registers, shared memory); blocks book them.
What occupancy enables: enough parallel work to cover memory latency.

recall.question: Define occupancy.
recall.answer: Occupancy = active warps / max warps per SM, limited by threads/SM, registers/thread, and shared memory/block.

recall.question: 256-thread blocks, 12 KB shared per block (toy: 100 KB/SM, 64 max warps). Occupancy?
recall.answer: 8 blocks fit (threads, shared, and registers all allow 8): 8 * 8 = 64 warps = 100%.

recall.question: Occupancy 100% but slow. Name two other suspects.
recall.answer: Low instruction-level parallelism with stalls, or register spilling. Occupancy is a means, not a goal.

keyTerms.definition: Parallel sum: pairs combine each round, halving the field.
The mental model: 1024 -> 512 -> ... -> 1 in 10 rounds.
The round count: 1024 needs 10 rounds.

recall.question: Rounds for N = 4096?
recall.answer: 12 rounds (log2(4096)).

recall.question: sum(0..4095) via the tree. Value?
Sum is wrong for odd N. Name the fix.
recall.answer: Pad: the code appends 0 when the length is odd, preserving the sum.

keyTerms.definition: O(T^2) HBM traffic from the score matrix: the bottleneck is bytes, not math.
4T^2n FLOPs over 4T^2 bytes = n = 64 FLOP/byte, below ridge 150: memory-bound.

recall.question: Name the four HBM trips.
recall.answer: Write scores, read for softmax, write probs, read for the values multiply: about 4 x 33.5 = 134 MB per head at T = 4096.

recall.question: T = 8192, h = 32, fp16. Score traffic bytes?
recall.answer: 4 * 8192^2 * 32 * 2 = 1.7e10 bytes (about 16 GiB) per layer.

recall.question: Attention at 90% DRAM bandwidth. What is the fix direction?
recall.answer: Cut bytes, not FLOPs: never materialize the T x T score matrix (FlashAttention, C10).

sections.title: C08: approximation versus exact IO savings

keyTerms.definition: Changing the math: sparse, low-rank, or kernel attention cut work but change the function.
Exact IO: FlashAttention computes the same thing with fewer HBM trips.
Attend to a subset, e.g. local window w: O(Tw) work.

recall.question: Name the three approximation families and one complexity each.
recall.answer: Sparse: O(Tw). Low-rank: O(Tr). Kernel: O(T).

recall.question: T = 8192, w = 512. Sparse work ratio?
Error budget is zero. Which family survives?
recall.answer: Exact IO (FlashAttention): the approximations change the model, exact IO keeps the address.

keyTerms.definition: Streaming softmax: one pass over row blocks with running (m, l).
The mental model: keep the max so far (m) and the running sum (l), rescaling as new blocks arrive.
The running row max.

recall.question: Write the (m, l) update.
recall.answer: m_b = max(x), l_b = sum(exp(x - m_b)). m' = max(m, m_b), l' = l exp(m - m') + l_b exp(m_b - m').

recall.question: Blocks [1,2],[3,100]. m' and l'?
recall.answer: m' = 100, l' about 1.0: softmax is about [0, 0, 0, 1].

recall.question: Probabilities do not sum to 1. Name the missing factor.
recall.answer: The rescale exp(m - m'): forgetting it gives l = 2.368 instead of 1.0 for the toy.

keyTerms.definition: Tiling plus online softmax: exact attention with O(T) HBM traffic.
The mental model: outer K/V loop, inner Q loop, score block computed on chip.
The running (m, l, o) statistics: the only thing that survives.

recall.question: Name the two loops and what each streams.
recall.answer: Outer loop streams K/V blocks (size Bc), inner loop streams Q blocks (size Br); each step holds one (Br, Bc) score block on chip.

recall.question: T = 4, Br = Bc = 2. Block pairs?
recall.answer: 2 Q blocks x 2 K/V blocks = 4 block pairs.

recall.question: Outputs match at T = 64 but not at T = 65. Name the suspect.
recall.answer: Tile-edge handling: causal masking or the last partial block at the block boundary.

keyTerms.definition: Rebuilding score tiles in the backward pass instead of storing them.
The mental model: throw away the prep bowls and re-chop; FLOPs are cheap, memory is scarce.
Backward memory with recompute, vs O(T^2) stored scores.

recall.question: What does the forward store, and what does the backward recompute?
recall.answer: Forward stores m, l (O(T)), not scores. Backward recomputes S tiles from Q, K blocks, then the dQ, dK, dV updates.

recall.question: T = 4096. Stored numbers: scores vs (m, l)?
recall.answer: Scores: 16.7M numbers. (m, l): 8192 numbers.

recall.question: Backward OOMs but forward fits. Name the cause.
recall.answer: Something stores the T^2 scores: the backward path is not recomputing as designed.

keyTerms.definition: Warmup runs before timing, so compile and first-run effects do not pollute the numbers.
Synchronized timing: device synchronize before/after, so time measures work, not launch.
Median of 100 beats mean of 3: outliers do not get a vote.

recall.question: Name the five rules.
recall.answer: Same shapes/dtype/hardware, warmup, device synchronize before/after, report median-of-N, include the baseline's best config.

recall.question: Times [5, 50, 51, 49, 200] us. Mean vs median. Which do you report?
recall.answer: Mean 71, median 50. Report the median.

recall.question: 9x claim, no sync in the script. What happened?
recall.answer: Time without sync measures launch, not work: the no-sync fake 9x. Follow the checklist.

keyTerms.definition: The thing never to materialize: naive attention's score matrix.
Tiled, online softmax, exact: the right side of the plate.

recall.question: What does the unit chapter plate contrast?
recall.answer: Naive attention (three kernels, T^2 HBM trips) vs the IO-aware algorithm (tiled, online softmax, exact). Bottom line: never materialize the T x T matrix.

keyTerms.definition: The Shell 0 question: can attention be exact with O(T) HBM traffic?
The online softmax rescale (C09).

recall.question: What is the Shell 3 rule of the FlashAttention ladder?
recall.answer: The online softmax rescale (C09).

recall.question: What breaks the ladder (Shell 7)?
recall.answer: Breaking the SRAM fit: blocks too big, the kernel cannot launch.

keyTerms.definition: Decides the serving kernel per context length (LLM engineer).
C09: the debugging tool for any attention kernel.

recall.question: What decides the serving kernel per context length?
recall.answer: The T* crossover: FlashAttention wins past it, naive wins below it.
